title: Arbitrary pullback of generation opens and specified Proj fraction maps
statement: Let $f:W\to T$, $f':W'\to T'$, $h:W'\to W$ and $g:T'\to T$ be scheme morphisms [def-pc-scheme] with $f\circ h=g\circ f'$; the square need not be cartesian. Let $\mathcal A$ be a quasi-coherent graded commutative $\mathcal O_T$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra, def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures], let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_W$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and let $\psi:f^*\mathcal A\to\bigoplus_{d\geq0}L^{\otimes d}$ be a graded algebra map. Set $\mathcal A'=g^*\mathcal A$, $L'=h^*L$, and let $\psi'$ be the pulled-back map, using tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Write $G\subseteq W$ and $G'\subseteq W'$ for the unions of the positive-degree stalkwise surjectivity loci. Then $G'=h^{-1}G$. More precisely, on affine trivializing charts $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq W$ over $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq T$ and $\operatorname{Spec}B'\subseteq W'$ over $\operatorname{Spec}R'\subseteq T'$ mapping into them, put $A=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathcal A)$. Let $e$ be a frame of $L$ on $\operatorname{Spec}B$ and use the frame $h^*e$ of $L'$ on $\operatorname{Spec}B'$. If $\psi(a)=\alpha_a e^{\otimes d}$, the coefficients relative to $(h^*e)^{\otimes d}$ of the images of $a\otimes c\in A\otimes_RR'$ are $h^\sharp(\alpha_a)f'^\sharp(c)$. The inverse images of the opens $D(\alpha_a)$ cover $G'$ on these charts. For any scheme morphisms $q:G\to\operatorname{Proj}_T(\mathcal A)$ and $q':G'\to\operatorname{Proj}_{T'}(\mathcal A')$ [def-nagata-relative-proj] specified on generator opens by $b/a^m\mapsto\psi(b)/\psi(a)^m$ and its primed version [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero], one has $c\circ q'=q\circ h|_{G'}$, where $c$ is the comparison to $\operatorname{Proj}_T(\mathcal A)$ of [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-base-change-arbitrary]. On each pulled-back generator chart the common ring map sends $b/a^m$ to $h^\sharp(\alpha_b)/h^\sharp(\alpha_a)^m$. No flatness or finite-generation hypothesis is required.

proof.text: On a fixed affine base V and affine frame chart B, apply [lem-trf-affine-tensor-generator-locus] to each positive degree. Quasi-coherence of each graded piece follows by expressing it as the kernel of identity minus the projector onto that piece. Thus the positive-degree stalk-surjectivity open restricted to B is the union of the coefficient basic opens. The existing atlas [lem-trf-line-proj-affine-chart-atlas] supplies its uniquely fraction-characterized chart maps and frame coefficient formula.

source.place: Tag 01O9 (lemma-invertible-map-into-relative-proj), preceding description of U(psi); Tag 01NK (lemma-invertible-map-into-proj), generator-open characterization

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] to express sections of the primed degree in finite sums of scalar multiples of pulled-back sections. Naturality of the section-normalized adjunction gives the pure-section formula through composition, equality transport and the pulled-back module map. The four equality-pinned components [def-trf-line-proj-comparison-components] equal the original maps. The recursive unit and tensor normalization [def-sc-tensor-pullback-power-comparison] sends the tensor power of a frame to the tensor power of its pullback. Restricting to B' gives coefficient h-sharp(alpha_a) times f'-sharp(c). Pullback of a free generator follows by transporting the usual pullback-unit frame through the normalized comparison.

source.place: Tag 0D2Z (lemma-invertible-map-into-relative-proj), (3): pulled-back map; tensor coefficient calculation expanding the omitted proof

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-affine-tensor-generator-locus] to the primed degree. The finite tensor expansion of its section has coefficient a sum of multiples of h-sharp(alpha_a). If all such coefficient germs were nonunits, all summands and their sum would lie in the maximal ideal of the local ring, contradicting generation. Conversely a unit coefficient gives a generator using a tensor with scalar one. Basic opens commute with arbitrary scheme inverse image. This proves the local pulled-back cover. Refine around each point by affine opens and a frame to conclude G'=h inverse G.

source.place: Tag 0D2Z (lemma-invertible-map-into-relative-proj), opening pullback assertion and (3); explicit local-ring verification

proof.text: On the pulled-back coefficient basic open, restrict the specified primed fraction map to its homogeneous localization chart. The coefficientwise comparison [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-base-change-arbitrary] is Proj.map of D.map on affine charts. Mathlib Proj.awayι_comp_map and HomogeneousLocalization.Away.map_mk identify its localization restriction and send b/a^m to D(b)/D(a)^m. Membership in the homogeneous grade supplies b from the corresponding module section. Apply the coefficient identity and the primed fraction formula and compare with the unprimed chart formula pulled back by h. The denominator coefficient is a unit on this open, so the scalar maps agree on all fractions, including m=0.

source.place: Tag 01O9 (lemma-invertible-map-into-relative-proj), affine characterization; Tag 01N2 (lemma-base-change-map-proj), coefficientwise chart comparison; Tag 01NK, degree-zero fraction formula

proof.text: Mathlib HomogeneousLocalization.Away.mk_surjective represents every degree-zero element by a homogeneous fraction. Cancel the unit denominator coefficient to deduce equality of the scalar maps; ext_to_Spec then gives equality of the chart morphisms. These pulled-back basic opens cover G' by step 3, so openCoverOfIsOpenCover.hom_ext gives the global commuting square. Restricting this equality and pulling back the unprimed coefficient fraction formula gives the asserted common factorizations and cross-multiplied scalar equation. Affine opens are chosen inside arbitrary intersections; intersections themselves need not be affine.
